newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia strike lifted, work to restart Friday.
newsitem.headline: Colombia strike lifted, work to restart Friday.

text.p: Dock workers lifted their nine-day-old strike at Colombia's main Pacific coast port late on Thursday after hammering out a deal that should more than double their wages, a union official said.

Ship owners and cargo handling operators decided not to begin loading and unloading waiting ships at the port of Buenaventura on Thursday night but agreed work should restart Friday morning, Nelson Amaya, regional head of the Unitary Workers' Confederation (CUT) said. The main dock workers' union is affiliated to the CUT.

The stoppage at the port of Buenaventura had paralysed 60 percent of the country's high-earning coffee exports, all its sugar exports and about 60 percent of all foreign trade, the port authorities said. They estimated the port had lost between $700,000 and $1 million for every day the strike lasted.

"Today's deal is an historic achievement. The port workers' had everything to gain and nothing to lose," Amaya told Reuters in a phone interview from the port. "For the first time, workers will be paid standard rates and will be protected from unfair competition," he added.

The deal reached with cargo and ship owners and cargo handling operators in the provincial capital Cali earlier in the day, set minimum rates to be paid to dockers depending on the type of cargo they were handling.

The accord also obliges those who contract their services to pay them social security, sickness and injury contributions and establishes a fixed eight hour working day with provision for overtime pay and meal allowances.
Amaya said in effect the deal would allow dock workers to earn about $200 per month, up from the current average of about $80 per month. The minimum wage in Colombia, as of January 1, is about $172.

A port authority spokeswoman said it would take at least five days to clear the backlog of cargo that had been snarled in the strike, including at least 305,000 60-kg bags of coffee exports and 27,000 tonnes of sack and bulk sugar.
Amaya said the dock workers would restart work after a short meeting scheduled for 0800 local (1300 GMT) Friday.
A port spokesman said 15 ships were docked or anchored in the port, more than 600 trucks were waiting to offload and more than 1,800 containers had been blocked by the strike.
